# Evaluating $\int_0^{1000} \frac{e^{-10x}\sin x}{x}\,dx$

## Identifying the Key Structure

The factor $e^{-10x}$ decays so rapidly that the integrand is negligible beyond even $x \approx 1$ (since $e^{-10} \approx 4.5\times 10^{-5}$). The upper limit of 1000 is far beyond where any contribution exists, so I can extend to $\infty$:

$$\int_0^{1000}\frac{e^{-10x}\sin x}{x}\,dx \approx \int_0^{\infty}\frac{e^{-10x}\sin x}{x}\,dx$$

**Truncation error bound:**
$$\left|\int_{1000}^{\infty}\frac{e^{-10x}\sin x}{x}\,dx\right| \le \frac{1}{1000}\int_{1000}^{\infty}e^{-10x}\,dx = \frac{e^{-10000}}{10000} \approx 0$$

This is astronomically smaller than $10^{-5}$.

## Computing the Improper Integral

Define $F(a) = \int_0^{\infty} \frac{e^{-ax}\sin x}{x}\,dx$ for $a>0$. Differentiating under the integral sign:

$$F'(a) = -\int_0^{\infty} e^{-ax}\sin x\,dx = -\frac{1}{a^2+1}$$

Since $F(\infty)=0$, I recover:

$$F(a) = \int_a^{\infty}\frac{dt}{t^2+1} = \frac{\pi}{2}-\arctan(a) = \arctan\!\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)$$

Setting $a=10$:

$$\int_0^{\infty}\frac{e^{-10x}\sin x}{x}\,dx = \arctan\!\left(\frac{1}{10}\right)$$

## Numerical Evaluation

Using the Maclaurin series $\arctan z = z - \frac{z^3}{3}+\frac{z^5}{5}-\frac{z^7}{7}+\cdots$ with $z=0.1$:

| Term | Value |
|------|-------|
| $+0.1$ | $0.1000000000$ |
| $-\frac{0.001}{3}$ | $-0.0003333333$ |
| $+\frac{10^{-5}}{5}$ | $+0.0000020000$ |
| $-\frac{10^{-7}}{7}$ | $-0.0000000143$ |
| $+\frac{10^{-9}}{9}$ | $+0.0000000001$ |
| $\cdots$ | $<10^{-10}$ |

$$\arctan(0.1) = 0.0996686525\ldots$$

## Final Check

$$|0.09967 - 0.0996686525| = 1.35\times 10^{-6} \;<\; 10^{-5} \;\checkmark$$

$$\boxed{0.09967}$$
